---
title: Upload from the command line
description: Push files and whole folders from a terminal, with the server's clipmux binary or with npx @clipmux/node from your app's project.
---

Two commands upload from a terminal. `npx @clipmux/node upload` runs in your
app's project and uses the credentials `init` wrote, which makes it the
quick way to test an integration. `clipmux push` is the server's own binary:
it walks folders, resumes an interrupted push, and with `--local` encodes on
a PC you own without uploading the file.

Both send the file in 32 MiB parts straight to storage, through the same
upload API a browser uses.

## Before you start

- For `npx @clipmux/node upload`: Node 20.19 or later, and an env file
  from `npx @clipmux/node init` with `CLIPMUX_URL` and `CLIPMUX_API_KEY`.
- For `clipmux push`: the `clipmux` binary, your server's URL, and an API
  key with `uploads:write` (and `assets:read` for `--wait`). For `--local`,
  a PC connected as a worker; see
  [Encode on a PC you own](/docs/self-host/encoding/your-pc).

## npx @clipmux/node upload

```bash
npx @clipmux/node upload lesson-42.mp4 --passthrough lesson_42 --wait
```

```txt
  0%
  10%
  …
✓ uploaded lesson-42.mp4: asset ast_… (processing)
Waiting until it is ready…
✓ ready: 1830.4 s, playback ID pid_…
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--passthrough REF` | Your own ID for the video. |
| `--title TITLE` | The video's title. Default: the file's name. |
| `--renditions LIST` | The rungs to encode, comma separated, for example `1080p,480p`. Default: every rung up to the source. |
| `--public` | Make a public playback ID instead of a private (`signed`) one. |
| `--wait` | Wait until the video is ready, and print its duration and playback ID. |
| `--env FILE` | Where to read the credentials. Default: `.env.local`, or `.env` if it exists. |

It uploads one file per run.

## clipmux push

The API key comes from `CLIPMUX_API_KEY`, never from a flag, so it doesn't
show in a process listing. The server URL comes from `--server` or
`CLIPMUX_SERVER`.

```bash
export CLIPMUX_API_KEY=cmx_…
clipmux push --server https://video.example.com --passthrough lesson_42 lesson-42.mp4
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--server URL` | `CLIPMUX_SERVER` | Your server's public URL. |
| `--policy POLICY` | `signed` | `signed` for a private video, `public` for a public one, or `signed,public` for one ID of each. |
| `--passthrough REF` | | Your own ID for the video. One file only. |
| `--renditions LIST` | every rung up to the source | The rungs to encode, comma separated, for example `1080p,480p`. |
| `--wait` | `false` | Wait until each video is ready. Needs an API key. |
| `--quiet` | `false` | Don't print the progress lines. |
| `--local` | `false` | Keep the files on this PC: its worker encodes them and uploads only the outputs. |
| `--upload-source` | `false` | With `--local`: once a video is encoded, also upload its file, so any worker can encode it again. |

### Folders

Give it folders as well as files. It walks each folder, skips folders whose
names start with a dot, and picks up files with these extensions: `.mp4`,
`.m4v`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.avi`, `.mxf`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.m2ts`,
`.flv`, `.wmv`, `.mpg`, `.mpeg`, `.ogv` and `.3gp`.

```bash
clipmux push --server https://video.example.com ./course/
```

`--passthrough` names one video, so push files one at a time to set it.

### URLs

A URL in place of a file is imported: the server fetches it, with the same
flags, and the API key needs `assets:write` for it. Files and URLs can be
mixed in one push, and the same import run again creates nothing new.
`npx @clipmux/node upload` takes a URL the same way. See
[Import from a URL](/docs/build/upload/from-url).

```bash
clipmux push --server https://video.example.com https://files.example.com/lesson-42.mp4
```

### Resuming

If a push is interrupted, run the same command again: it resumes where it
stopped. Pushing a file that has already finished creates nothing new.
`clipmux push` keeps what it needs for this in your user cache folder, or in
`CLIPMUX_PUSH_STATE_DIR`.

### Output

Progress goes to standard error, one line per file. Standard output gets one
tab-separated line per video: its asset ID, its playback ID, its status and
the file's path, so you can pipe it into other tools.

```txt
ast_…	pid_…	processing	course/lesson-42.mp4
```

The exit code is `0` when every file went through, `1` if any failed or
ended `errored`, and `2` for a usage mistake.

### --local

With `--local`, the file never leaves the PC. The PC's connected worker
encodes it in place and uploads only the encrypted outputs. With an API key
the key's app owns the video; without one, it becomes the server owner's
own upload, as from the dashboard, and `--server` isn't needed.

Such a video can be encoded again only on that PC, because its source is
there. Add `--upload-source` to upload the file once it is encoded, so any
worker can re-encode it later.

## Check it works

The last line of `npx @clipmux/node upload --wait` names the playback ID,
and `clipmux push --wait` prints `ready` as the status. Without `--wait`,
your webhook receives `video.asset.ready` when encoding is done.

- `unauthorized`: the API key is wrong or revoked.
- `insufficient_scope`: the key lacks `uploads:write`, or `assets:read` for
  `--wait`.
- `too_large`: the file is over the server's upload limit.
- `clipmux push: needs --server and CLIPMUX_API_KEY (or --local), and at least one file`:
  set both, or use `--local`.
- `no video files found`: the folder has no file with one of the extensions
  above.
